plugging.note: plugging = 1.5 x the contacts' sliding forces (p.135) plus the four couplings' springs (43 and 44.5 N without pressure, p.73, p.75) plus, with vacuum, the UCT08 pair's maximum sliding force at 0 bar (16 N, p.67; no spring); every coupling is vented to atmosphere before mating and parting, so no pressure term; evacuated, the vacuum coupling pulls the halves together, which only helps the dead centre hold; the crank's torque is the worst over the last 15 mm of travel, where everything engages

plugging_without_vacuum.note: plugging = 1.5 x the contacts' sliding forces (p.135) plus the four couplings' springs (43 and 44.5 N without pressure, p.73, p.75) plus, with vacuum, the UCT08 pair's maximum sliding force at 0 bar (16 N, p.67; no spring); every coupling is vented to atmosphere before mating and parting, so no pressure term; evacuated, the vacuum coupling pulls the halves together, which only helps the dead centre hold; the crank's torque is the worst over the last 15 mm of travel, where everything engages

trays.B: the vacuum press (vacuum_press.py): its evacuable die is pumped below 1 mbar for 2 min before pressing; the line replaces the rotary-vane pump drawn beside the press
trays.K: the glovebox (instruments_r7.py): three pump-and-N2-refill cycles of its 150 x 300 mm mini antechamber (about 5.3 L) for every transfer; the line replaces the pump in the glovebox's bay
trays.M: the S2 PUMA XRF (instruments_char.py): Bruker lists air, vacuum, He or N2, and a 'Helium mode with reduced pressure' for loose powder; vacuum needs a pump (and presumably so does the reduced-pressure mode), which the line provides instead of Bruker's own

vacuum.bay: always: the bay's dock carries the vacuum plug for whichever of these trays it is presented
vacuum.others: every other powered tray: the same carrier, empty, its bore blind-plugged at the back; its slot's dock has an empty carrier and no vacuum block
sequence: mating: the tray's valve and the dock's isolation valve are shut, the stretch between them at atmosphere (vented with N2 when it last parted); the O-ring seals with 3.5 mm to go, after air and N2 open and before the LMFB pair

mated (LMFB loop closed): the isolation valve opens, slowly at first, and pumps the stretch up to the tray's valve; the gauge shows it falling; the tray's valve opens when the instrument asks for vacuum, and the tray's line and the instrument are pumped through it

before letting go: the instrument's own vent (the press's V2, the antechamber's refill) brings it up with dry gas, the tray's valve shuts, the isolation valve shuts (the riser stays under vacuum), the vent valve lets N2 into the stretch between the two valves until the gauge reads atmospheric, then the head pulls back

line.what: the tray's line, 10 x 8 mm, to the instrument
the dock's tube through the energy chain
DN16 branch, isolation valve to the riser
DN25 riser and run to the pump

line.method: each element a round tube, its conductance the laminar plus the molecular term (Leybold eq. 1.28a, 1.28b, air at 20 C); the pressure marched from the pump's inlet to the tray for each throughput; the pump's speed taken as S0 (1 - p_ult / p); pump-down times by integrating V dp / (Q(p) - Q0); fittings, valves and bends not counted

line.turbo: at 1e-5 mbar the gas is in molecular flow and the whole line conducts what 'molecular_conductance_whole_line_l_s' gives, a few hundredths of a litre per second: even a clean chamber's 1e-5 mbar l/s would sit at 'best_at_1e_5...' mbar, however big the pump. A turbo at the tray pumps the chamber at its own 10-35 l/s and needs only its foreline below its maximum (HiPace 10/30/80: 25, 24, 22 mbar; nEXT85: 18), which the line holds at the 'turbo_foreline...' value. A leak at the coupling only adds to the foreline's gas load, which the turbo's compression (3e6 for N2, HiPace 10) keeps off the chamber; the foreline could even be held above the coupling's 14 mbar rating.
